daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The National Police scheduled an ethics hearing for General Listyo Sigit for next week, following the ongoing wiretapping scandal involving President Prabowo. The case expanded as Bareskrim Polri raided Irjen Eko Hadi's house in Cipete, which had been used as a wiretapping post against Prabowo and others, while LPSK continued to examine protection requests from eight witnesses in the case. The scandal has prompted calls for stronger oversight mechanisms for state surveillance powers.

  • The DPR reached final stages on the Asset Forfeiture Bill, moving forward with legislative efforts to strengthen anti-corruption measures.
  • PSI chairperson Grace Natalie confirmed the party supports the Prabowo administration despite having no ministers in the cabinet, clarifying the party's political position in the current coalition.
  • The Election Law faces a new Constitutional Court challenge seeking to lower the minimum age for presidential and vice-presidential candidates to 19 years.
  • Commission I of the DPR proposed an artificial intelligence bill for inclusion in the National Legislation Program, addressing emerging technology governance.
  • Vice President Ma'ruf Amin denied any decision to build a Sekolah Rakyat in a forest area, responding to recent controversy over the education project's location.
  • The KPK questioned 16 district heads in Klaten to investigate money received from Bupati Hamenang Wajar Ismoyo in a corruption probe.
  • The KPK responded to Raffi Ahmad's claims about consultations in 2024, addressing the celebrity's statements regarding interactions with the anti-corruption agency.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo attended the ASEAN-US Special Summit alongside US President Trump, in a high-level diplomatic engagement. The president also urged the East Asia Summit to cooperate on Indo-Pacific stability and reaffirmed Indonesia's support for Palestine during the same forum.

  • A senior DPR lawmaker urged the president to intensify Indonesia's diplomatic efforts on Palestine, calling for stronger advocacy at international forums.
  • Indonesia pushed for stronger ASEAN-India maritime cooperation and connectivity, advancing regional partnership initiatives.
  • President Prabowo praised India's pharmaceutical industry and medical technology during bilateral discussions, highlighting potential areas for cooperation.
  • Indonesia was elected as a member of the UN Telecommunications Council for the 2027-2030 period, securing a seat in the international body.
  • Indonesia is set to receive an Airbus A340-500 aircraft from Türkiye, involving bilateral defence or government cooperation.

Other

The government assured that Ujung Kulon National Park is not designated as a mining area, addressing environmental concerns after controversy over proposals to relocate Javan rhinos. Environmental group WALHI questioned the relocation plan and its possible connection to gold mining interests, while a DPR member insisted the rhinos should remain in Banten.

  • Indonesia launched three blue carbon projects at COP31, advancing climate mitigation efforts through marine ecosystem conservation.
  • Indonesia's Kadin brought 80 businesspeople to China on a trade mission to strengthen economic ties and explore investment opportunities.
  • The government is pushing to end food import dependence, pursuing greater self-sufficiency in agricultural production.
  • Indonesia accelerated clean energy projects through AZEC 2.0, implementing an updated framework for renewable energy development.
  • The Health Ministry called for increased domestic medical device production to reduce import dependence in the healthcare sector.
